name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+11 PVI) in reliably blue Massachusetts
Koh's roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge plus outside support with none opposing him
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96%
Open seat removes incumbency, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Dan Koh's dominant fundraising and outside backing, and market pricing near 96% all point to a safe hold despite Seth Moulton's retirement. Nothing in the evidence suggests Republican Micah Jones has the resources or profile to make this competitive.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly strong Jones campaign could narrow the margin, though a flip would require a dramatic shift in a district this blue.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Massachusetts' sixth district is firmly Democratic territory, and Seth Moulton's retirement to run for Senate leaves the seat open but hardly competitive. Dan Koh enters the general election with roughly ten times the fundraising of Republican Micah Jones, more than $2 million in cash on hand, and outside groups spending on his behalf while none oppose him. Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 96%.

The open seat removes the incumbent's personal vote, and the absence of general-election polling leaves some room for error. But the district's eleven-point Democratic lean, Koh's financial dominance, and the lack of any expert rating placing the race in play all point the same way. A Republican upset would require a dramatic shift; the more realistic question is the size of the Democratic margin in a low-information race.
